items.title: Labarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: all the stuff I had learned at Berklee and then with Herb Pomeroy and Ray Santisi, Charlie Mariano

ctx.x: I never thought I’d be — my father was a music teacher. I helped my music teacher in the school teach younger kids clarinet, never thought about teaching. Went to Potsdam State

Teacher’s College and never thought about teaching. Went to Berklee, it never crossed my mind. I moved to Canada in ’74 and I was with Yamaha at the time. I had signed with Yamaha in the States, the last couple of months with Buddy Rich and so when I came to Canada I was with Yamaha. And they called me and they said we’ve got this young student who is, they called him the “rising star” the Yamaha Rising Star Award. And we wondered if you’d give him a couple of lessons. I said gee, I never taught anybody. I don’t…

I said, you know I’m going to be, I’ve got to travel to make a living here because I’m not doing anything in town. And so that’s what happened. I got the job with Elvin and then I started to get more and more students each year but it was always part time until the 80s when they offered me a — in ’87 they offered me a full time position. So I was off and on with Elvin for almost twenty years plus. I would go out with him — ’75, ’76, ’77, ’78, ’79 — I was with him pretty much. Then I left for a bit, came back,…
